name: Li-ion Battery Separators & Cell Materials Localisation
scope: Indian listed companies localising Li-ion cell materials (separator film, anode, cathode, electrolyte/LiPF6, binder, foil) as domestic ACC gigafactories start up, plus the policy, customers, valuation and risks around them.

summary.one_line: Indian cell capacity has started to switch on (Exide's 6 GWh Phase-I was commissioned on 23 Sep 2026), but the materials that go into the cells are still mostly made in China. TCPL Packaging's Rs 125 cr separator-film project is the only listed separator entry we could confirm. It is small, starts with coating/conversion, has no named partner or customer yet, and targets production in Q4 FY28. The anode and electrolyte names are larger and further ahead, but their battery revenue is still negligible.
key_points: Exide Energy Solutions commissioned Phase-I (6 GWh) of its Devanahalli, Bengaluru cell plant on 23 Sep 2026. It will first replace imported LFP cells in its Gujarat pack plant for e-3Ws, then supply e-2W packs and NMC cells to OEMs by the end of FY27 (S5, S6).

On 11 Aug 2026 TCPL Packaging's board approved Rs 125 cr over 18 months for 70 million sq m a year of separator film, enough for about 6-8 GWh of cells. Commercial production is targeted for Q4 FY28 and the long-term ambition is 500 million sq m (about 50 GWh) over 5-7 years. The wholly-owned subsidiary TCPL Energy Materials Ltd was incorporated on 24 Sep 2026 (S1, S2, S3).

Supply is concentrated in China. IEA data cited by CSIS put China at 74% of separators, 82% of electrolytes and 85% of anodes. The IEA's 2025 battery report puts China at over 90% of anode materials, almost 85% of cathode materials and 80% of cell production (S9, S10).

The government is preparing an incentive of up to Rs 13,000 cr for anode and cathode active materials, electrolytes, separator film and copper foil. It is awaiting Expenditure Finance Committee approval. The Rs 18,100 cr ACC-PLI has awarded 40 GWh of its 50 GWh, and beneficiaries have reported delays (S8, S1).

Battery revenue is still tiny for the companies that have already re-rated. Gujarat Fluorochemicals' battery segment made Rs 14 cr of revenue with an EBITDA loss of Rs 30 cr in Q1 FY27, against group revenue of Rs 1,588 cr (S19). Himadri's anode plant has 200 MTPA of capacity against a stated 200,000 MT ambition (S13).

Over one year (screener.in, 30 Sep 2026) the stocks rose: Himadri +51%, Graphite India +39%, TCPL +20% and Gujarat Fluorochemicals +19%. Trailing P/Es are 42.8x, 68.2x, 30.9x and 78.3x respectively (S4, S15, S18, S21).

Media lists of battery-localisation stocks group Exide, Himadri and Neogen Chemicals. A Trade Brains list from Aug 2026 does not mention TCPL (S7), which is consistent with the separator leg being thinly covered.

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Early material makers with domestic cell customers that are now commissioning: Exide 6 GWh (S5), Amara Raja's 60 MWh qualification plant ahead of its 2 GWh Giga 1 in CY2027 (S24), and Ola, which is scaling towards 6 GWh (S25).
Electrolyte and salt makers with qualified product. GFL's LiPF6 is approved by most major global electrolyte makers (S20). Neogen guides to Rs 300 cr of FY27 battery revenue (S22).
Every material named in the proposed Rs 13,000 cr scheme, including separator film, if it is approved (S8).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Competition from imports: China's share of separators (74%) and anodes (85%+) means local plants compete with scaled incumbents (S9, S10).
Demand slippage: ACC-PLI beneficiaries have missed production milestones because of gaps in technology, skilled labour and components (S8).
Execution and qualification: TCPL plans about one year of qualification before supply and has no named technology partner or customer (S1, S2). GFL's battery business is still loss-making (S19, S20).
Funding: GFL's battery capex is Rs 2,300 cr in FY27 and Rs 6,000 cr cumulative to FY28, and it is still looking for funding after moving its Oman project to India (S19, S20).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Q2 FY27 results in October-November: GFL's target of three-digit quarterly battery revenue by Q4 FY27 (S19), Neogen's Ionics run-rate (S22), and TCPL disclosures on land, technology and equipment (S1).
Himadri's LFP cathode Phase-I, targeted for Q3 FY27 (S12).
Whether the Expenditure Finance Committee and Cabinet approve the cell-component incentive (S8).
Exide's ramp to e-2W and NMC supply by the end of FY27 (S5).

subsections.title: What a separator is and why it matters

blocks.text: A separator is a thin, porous polyolefin film that sits between a cell's anode and cathode. TCPL's wet-process route involves blending, extrusion, stretching, forming pores by solvent extraction, then coating, slitting, winding and testing (S1). The market is moving towards coated, multilayer separators for safety as regulations tighten (S11). ResearchAndMarkets values the global separator market at USD 8.0 bn in 2025 and forecasts USD 17.14 bn by 2031, a 13.54% CAGR. APAC, led by China, has about 55% of the market (S11).

TCPL's disclosure gives a rule of thumb: 70 million sq m of film supports about 6-8 GWh of cells, or roughly 9-12 million sq m per GWh (S1). On that ratio, Exide's 6 GWh Phase-I alone would need on the order of 50-70 million sq m a year, about the same as TCPL's whole first phase. This is our arithmetic on TCPL's ratio, not a company figure. The IEA says global battery demand passed 1 TWh in 2024 and expects more than 3 TWh by 2030 (S9).

subsections.title: Supply concentration and India's import dependence

blocks.caption: China's share of global Li-ion component production

blocks.text: The sources give different shares because they measure different years. The table shows both. Business Today reports that most Indian battery makers buy these materials from Chinese suppliers and that domestic cell makers have hit supply-chain bottlenecks (S8). The leading separator suppliers named by ResearchAndMarkets are SEMCORP (China), Asahi Kasei (Japan), SK Group (Korea) and W-SCOPE (S11).

items: ACC-PLI: Rs 18,100 cr outlay for 50 GWh. 40 GWh has been awarded to Reliance's renewable unit, Ola Electric and others (S1, S8).
ACC-PLI beneficiaries have been delayed in meeting production milestones because of gaps in technology availability, a shortage of skilled labour and components that were not available (S8).

Proposed cell-component incentive of up to Rs 13,000 cr (USD 1.37 bn) covering anode and cathode active materials, electrolytes, separator film and copper foil. Inter-ministerial consultation is done and it awaits Expenditure Finance Committee approval. No disbursement timeline has been published (S8).

blocks.text: The component scheme has not been approved yet (S8). TCPL's project economics as disclosed (Rs 150-200 cr revenue, 'good double-digit' margins) do not depend on it (S2).

blocks.text: TCPL describes itself as India's largest folding-carton maker (S4). In Q1 FY27 it reported total income of Rs 494.9 cr (+15.9% YoY), EBITDA margin of 17.8% and PAT of Rs 40.0 cr (+79.2%) (S2). The separator project is Rs 125 cr, funded from internal accruals and debt (S1), against a market cap of Rs 3,733 cr and borrowings of Rs 599 cr in Mar 2026 (S4). Management expects first-phase revenue of Rs 150-200 cr (S2).

Credibility check: TCPL is relying on its existing skills in specialised films, polymer processing and precision manufacturing (S1). Phase one is coating and conversion. It will only integrate backward into base-film manufacturing if demand accelerates (S2). The sources reviewed name no technology partner and no customer (S1, S2). The investment case therefore rests on qualification, which management expects to take about a year.

items: Himadri: FY26 revenue Rs 4,660.7 cr, EBITDA Rs 1,006 cr, PAT Rs 755 cr (+36%) (S12). Its anode plant at Mahistikry uses technology developed in-house over about a decade (S13). Himadri is negotiating LFP supply with global EV and battery makers. No qualification win has been disclosed in the sources reviewed (S14).

Graphite India: FY26 sales Rs 2,852 cr and net profit Rs 171 cr, with large other income of Rs 322 cr. It is close to debt-free, with borrowings of Rs 368 cr (S18). Its Rs 4,330 cr anode capex is several times its net profit (S16, S18).

Gujarat Fluorochemicals: battery revenue was Rs 11 cr in Q4 FY26 and Rs 14 cr in Q1 FY27, with EBITDA losses of Rs 45 cr and Rs 30 cr, against Q1 group revenue of Rs 1,588 cr. That makes battery revenue under 1% of the group. Management expects significant revenue traction late in FY27 and in FY28 (S19, S20).

Neogen Chemicals: Q1 FY27 Neogen Ionics revenue was Rs 19 cr. FY27 guidance is Rs 300 cr (Rs 200 cr salts, Rs 100 cr electrolyte for ACC-PLI cell makers). Its technology partners are Mitsubishi and Morita, and management says it has no technology dependence on China (S22).

sections.title: Research house views and market pricing

blocks.title: 1-year share price return
blocks.source: Source: screener.in, 30 Sep 2026 (S4, S15, S18, S21)

blocks.text: We could not confirm 6-month returns or the brief's GFL '+43% in 6 months' from the sources we opened, so they are left out. Some shorter-term moves can be confirmed. Himadri was Rs 753.50 on 4 Aug 2026 (S7) and Rs 678 on 30 Sep (S15). Graphite India rose 5.4% on the day of the Rs 4,330 cr anode approval (S16) and is now Rs 765 (S18).

Media lists of battery-localisation stocks cover Exide, Himadri and Neogen (Trade Brains, Aug 2026). TCPL is not in them (S7). Himadri held an investor meeting with Goldman Sachs on 28 Sep 2026 (S15). We found no broker initiation that groups TCPL with the materials names. We found no other listed Indian separator-film entrant either. The separator bucket is a single small cap, and that seems to reflect how early the niche is.

items: Chinese scale and pricing: China makes most separators, electrolytes and anodes, and battery pack prices fell 20% in 2024 (S9, S10).
Qualification delays: TCPL expects about a year of qualification (S2), GFL's LFP final qualification has slipped to Q3 FY27 (S20), and GFL's battery EBITDA is negative (S19).
Cell-demand slippage: ACC-PLI beneficiaries have missed milestones (S8).
Capex and leverage: GFL plans Rs 6,000 cr of battery capex to FY28 and has Rs 2,721 cr of borrowings (S20, S21). Graphite India's Rs 4,330 cr plan is to be funded partly with debt (S16).
Technology shift: the move to coated, multilayer separators (S11) raises the bar for a coating-first entrant. Alternative chemistries such as sodium-ion were not quantified in the sources reviewed.
TCPL Energy Materials: land, technology partner, equipment orders in 2026 and construction in 2027 (S1, S3).
Q2 FY27 results: GFL's battery revenue trajectory towards three-digit quarterly revenue by Q4 (S19); Neogen's commercial production at the Dahej replacement plant in Q2 FY27 (S22).
Himadri LFP Phase-I in Q3 FY27 (S12); GFL PVDF commercial start in H1 FY27 (S20).
Cabinet approval of the Rs 13,000 cr component scheme (S8).
Amara Raja's customer validation samples and Giga 1 start (S24); Exide's NMC and e-2W supply by the end of FY27 (S5).

companies.name: TCPL Packaging Ltd
companies.role: Folding-carton and films maker entering wet-process Li-ion separator film through TCPL Energy Materials Ltd: 70 mn sq m initial capacity, Rs 125 cr (S1, S3, S4).
companies.impact: This is a small option inside a Rs 3,733 cr company. It could add Rs 150-200 cr of revenue from Q4 FY28 if qualification succeeds. No partner or customer has been disclosed (S2, S4).

companies.name: Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd
companies.role: Coal-tar-pitch major. Commissioned a 200 MTPA anode material plant in Apr 2026 and is building LFP cathode capacity (2,000 MTPA Phase-I; Odisha plant) (S12, S13, S14).
companies.impact: Up 51% over one year at 42.8x P/E (S15). The battery business is still at pilot scale against a 200,000 MT ambition (S13).

companies.name: Graphite India Ltd
companies.role: Graphite electrode maker. Board approved Rs 4,330 cr for synthetic graphite anode materials on 28 Jan 2026 (S16).
companies.impact: Capex is large relative to FY26 net profit of Rs 171 cr. Low ROCE of 4.58% and 68.2x P/E (S18).

companies.name: Gujarat Fluorochemicals Ltd
companies.role: Fluoropolymer major building LiPF6, electrolyte, PVDF binder, LFP cathode and anode materials (S19, S20).
companies.impact: Battery revenue was Rs 14 cr in Q1 FY27 with an EBITDA loss of Rs 30 cr. Rs 6,000 cr of capex is planned to FY28. The stock trades at 78.3x P/E (S19, S20, S21).

companies.name: Neogen Chemicals Ltd
companies.role: Electrolyte and lithium-salt maker through Neogen Ionics, with Mitsubishi and Morita partnerships (S22).
companies.impact: Guides to Rs 300 cr of FY27 battery revenue, with Rs 100 cr of electrolyte going to ACC-PLI cell makers (S22).

companies.name: Hindalco Industries Ltd
companies.role: Commissioned India's first battery-grade aluminium foil plant (170 ktpa, supports up to 100 GWh) in Jan 2026 (S23).
companies.impact: Cathode current-collector foil is localised. The plant is immaterial to Hindalco's size but useful to domestic cell makers (S23).

companies.name: Exide Industries Ltd
companies.role: Cell maker through Exide Energy Solutions; 6 GWh Phase-I commissioned 23 Sep 2026 (S5, S6).
companies.impact: Exide is the first large domestic customer for local separators and other materials as it replaces imported cells (S5).

companies.name: Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Ltd
companies.role: Commissioned a 60 MWh cell qualification plant in Jul 2026; 2 GWh Giga 1 in CY2027 within a 16 GWh programme (S24).
companies.impact: A potential materials buyer from CY2027 (S24).

companies.name: Ola Electric Mobility Ltd
companies.role: ACC-PLI awardee making 4680 NMC and 46100 LFP cells, scaling towards 6 GWh (S8, S25).
companies.impact: A domestic cell demand source, though PLI milestone delays have been reported (S8).

companies.name: Reliance Industries Ltd
companies.role: Its renewable unit is an ACC-PLI capacity awardee (S8).
companies.impact: Potentially the largest future materials buyer. Delays have been reported across PLI beneficiaries (S8).

method: First edition, researched on 1 Oct 2026 with web search and page fetches. Company facts come from exchange-filing coverage, company releases and earnings-call summaries. Supply-concentration data comes from IEA as reported by CSIS and electrive. Market data comes from screener.in pages dated 30 Sep 2026. Several primary pages (PIB, IEA, Himadri's PDF) could not be read and were not cited. Claims we could not confirm were dropped: Graphite India's anode tonnage, 6-month returns, and country separator shares beyond China. We also searched for other listed separator entrants among BOPP/BOPET film makers and found none. No ratings or price targets are given.
